question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

O, M, ?, F, A, U, N, F
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. J.

GIVEN

• O, M, ?, F, A, U, N, F

SOLUTION

• Write position numbers (A=1 … Z=26): O(15), M(13), ?, F(6), A(1), U(21), N(14), F(6).

• The gap between consecutive terms grows by one each step: −2, −3, −4, −5, −6, −7, −8.

• 15−2=13(M); 13−3=10(J); 10−4=6(F); 6−5=1(A); 1−6=−5→21(U); 21−7=14(N); 14−8=6(F).

• So the missing term = position 10 = J.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Check the differences of position numbers; here they form −2,−3,−4… so the missing one is 13−3=10=J.

NOTE

• For alphabet series, convert letters to numbers (A=1…Z=26) and hunt for an arithmetic pattern in the differences.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

? , PQ, VV, ZZ, FE, JI, PN, TR
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. LM.

GIVEN

• ? , PQ, VV, ZZ, FE, JI, PN, TR

SOLUTION

• First letters: P(16), V(22), Z(26), F(32), J(36), P(42), T(46) → pattern +6, +4, +6, +4… so the term before P is P−4 = L.

• Second letters: Q(17), V(22), Z(26), E(31), I(35), N(40), R(44) → pattern +5, +4, +5, +4… so the term before Q is Q−4 = M.

• Missing term = LM.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Split each cluster into its two columns; both columns rise steadily, so step backward one place from PQ → LM.

NOTE

• In two-letter series, always separate the first and second letters and solve each column independently.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

JK, HH, FE, ?, BY, ZV, XS, VP
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. DB.

GIVEN

• JK, HH, FE, ?, BY, ZV, XS, VP

SOLUTION

• First letters: J(10), H(8), F(6), ?, B(2), Z(26), X(24), V(22) → decreasing by 2, so ? = 6−2 = 4 = D.

• Second letters: K(11), H(8), E(5), ?, Y(25), V(22), S(19), P(16) → decreasing by 3, so ? = 5−3 = 2 = B.

• Missing term = DB.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• First column −2, second column −3; from FE step down to DB.

NOTE

• Steadily decreasing letter series: negative differences; keep column-wise tracking to avoid slips near the A/Z wrap.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fifth letter cluster in the same way as the second letter cluster is related to the first letter cluster and fourth letter cluster is related to third letter cluster.

BA : UZ :: JH : CS :: NO : ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. GL.

GIVEN

• BA : UZ :: JH : CS :: NO : ?

SOLUTION

• First letter rule: subtract 7. B(2)−7=U(21); J(10)−7=C(3); N(14)−7=G(7).

• Second letter rule: take the opposite letter (27−x). A(1)→Z(26); H(8)→S(19); O(15)→27−15=12=L.

• So NO → GL.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Check the second letters are opposites (sum 27) and the first letters drop by 7; apply both to NO.

NOTE

• Opposite letter pairs sum to 27 (A–Z, B–Y, …); very common in SSC analogy clusters.

question:
In the following question, set of letter clusters are given. The letter clusters of each set are related to the letter clusters of the same set by some Logic/Rule/Relation. From the given alternatives, select a group of letter clusters which follows the same Logic/Rule/Relation.

(TL, XP, BT)

(NY, RC, VG)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (VF, ZJ, DN).

GIVEN

• (TL, XP, BT) and (NY, RC, VG)

SOLUTION

• Within a valid set, going from one cluster to the next BOTH letters advance by +4. TL→XP→BT: T,X,B (+4) and L,P,T (+4). NY→RC→VG: N,R,V (+4) and Y,C,G (+4).

• Test the options: Option 1 (VF, ZJ, DN): V,Z,D (+4) and F,J,N (+4) ✓.

• Option 2 N,R,Y = +4,+7 ✗; Option 3 C,G,I = +4,+2 ✗; Option 4 Z,D,I = +4,+5 ✗.

• Only (VF, ZJ, DN) follows +4/+4.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Just check that both letters jump +4 from cluster to cluster; the odd sets break at the second step.

NOTE

• For 'pick the matching set' questions, find the internal rule of the sample set first, then screen options quickly.

question: What was the day of the week on 14 February 2019?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Thursday.

GIVEN

• Find the day on 14 February 2019.

SOLUTION

• 1 January 2019 was a Tuesday.

• Day number of 14 Feb = 31 (Jan) + 14 = 45th day of the year.

• Odd days from day 1 to day 45 = (45−1) mod 7 = 44 mod 7 = 2.

• Tuesday + 2 = Thursday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Remember 1 Jan 2019 = Tuesday; add (45−1) mod 7 = 2 days → Thursday.

NOTE

• Anchoring one known date of the year and counting odd days is faster than the full odd-days-of-century method.

question: A person was born on 19 August 2015. What day of the week will be on his 8th birthday?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Saturday.

GIVEN

• Born 19 August 2015; find the day on the 8th birthday (19 August 2023).

SOLUTION

• 19 August 2015 was a Wednesday.

• From 2015 to 2023 = 8 years; leap years crossed (Feb 29) = 2016 and 2020 → 2 extra days.

• Total odd days = 8 + 2 = 10 → 10 mod 7 = 3.

• Wednesday + 3 = Saturday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Odd days = number of years + number of Feb-29s in the span = 8 + 2 = 10 ≡ 3; shift 3 days ahead.

NOTE

• A leap day counts only if 29 February actually falls inside the date range.

question: 5 persons V, M, N, P and Q are sitting in a row facing north (not necessarily in the same order). Two persons sit between P and M. P is to the left of M. Two persons sit between V and Q. V is to the left of M and to the right of P. How many persons are sitting to the right of V?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 3.

GIVEN

• 5 in a row (facing north). Two between P and M, P left of M. Two between V and Q. V is right of P and left of M.

SOLUTION

• Two between P and M with P left ⇒ P at seat 1, M at seat 4.

• V is right of P and left of M, and two sit between V and Q ⇒ V at seat 2, Q at seat 5.

• Remaining N takes seat 3. Order (left→right): P, V, N, M, Q.

• Persons right of V (seat 2) = N, M, Q = 3.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Fix the widest clue first (P and M three seats apart), then slot V between them; V lands 2nd, leaving 3 to its right.

NOTE

• 'Two persons between X and Y' means X and Y are 3 seats apart (positions differ by 3).

question: Marks of 6 girls P, Q, R, S, T and U are compared. Marks of no two girls are same. Marks of P are not less than anyone. Marks of U and R both are more than both S and T but less than Q. Marks of U and R are 300 and 400 respectively. What will be the possible marks of S?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 280.

GIVEN

• P ≥ everyone (so P highest). U, R > both S and T, but U, R < Q. U = 300, R = 400.

SOLUTION

• S is less than both U (300) and R (400), so S < 300.

• Check options: 350, 390, 320 are all ≥ 300 → not allowed; only 280 < 300.

• So possible marks of S = 280.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• S must be below the smaller of U and R (i.e. below 300); only 280 qualifies.

NOTE

• In inequality ranking, pin each variable against its nearest bound; the answer must satisfy the tightest limit.

question: 7 girls P, Q, R, S, T, U and V are sitting in a row facing north (not necessarily in the same order). U sits second from left end of the row. R is third to the right of V. T sits third from right end of the row. R is to the immediate left of T. Q is fourth to the right of S. How many girls are sitting to the right of V?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 6.

GIVEN

• 7 seats. U = 2nd from left (seat 2). T = 3rd from right (seat 5). R immediately left of T (seat 4). R is 3rd right of V. Q is 4th right of S.

SOLUTION

• R at seat 4 and R is 3rd right of V ⇒ V at seat 1.

• Remaining seats 3, 6, 7 for P, Q, S. Q = 4th right of S ⇒ S at 3, Q at 7; then P at 6.

• Order (left→right): V, U, S, R, T, P, Q.

• Girls right of V (seat 1) = seats 2–7 = 6.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• V ends up at the extreme left, so everyone else (6 girls) is to its right.

NOTE

• 'kth from right end' in an n-seat row = seat (n−k+1); here 3rd from right in 7 seats = seat 5.

question:
Select the option that is related to the first letter-number cluster in the same way as the fourth letter-number cluster is related to the third letter-number cluster and sixth letter-number cluster is related to fifth letter-number cluster. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

TU200 : ? :: ZP300 : YS540 :: KO500 : JR740
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. SX440.

GIVEN

• TU200 : ? :: ZP300 : YS540 :: KO500 : JR740

SOLUTION

• Study a known pair, ZP300 → YS540: Z(26)−1=Y(25); P(16)+3=S(19); 300+240=540.

• Confirm with KO500 → JR740: K(11)−1=J(10); O(15)+3=R(18); 500+240=740. Rule = (−1, +3, +240).

• Apply to TU200: T(20)−1=S(19); U(21)+3=X(24); 200+240=440 → SX440.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• First letter −1, second letter +3, number +240; feed TU200 through it.

NOTE

• Derive the rule from the fully given pair, then apply the SAME rule to the unknown pair.

question:
Select the option that is related to the first letter-number cluster in the same way as the fourth letter-number cluster is related to the third letter-number cluster and sixth letter-number cluster is related to fifth letter-number cluster. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

DF100 : ? :: KR300 : QJ260 :: LT400 : SK360
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. EC60.

GIVEN

• DF100 : ? :: KR300 : QJ260 :: LT400 : SK360

SOLUTION

• KR300 → QJ260: reverse KR to RK, then each letter −1 → QJ (R−1=Q, K−1=J); number 300−40=260.

• Check LT400 → SK360: reverse LT to TL, each −1 → SK (T−1=S, L−1=K); 400−40=360. Rule = reverse + (−1 each), number −40.

• Apply to DF100: reverse DF to FD, each −1 → EC (F−1=E, D−1=C); 100−40=60 → EC60.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Swap the two letters, step each back by 1, subtract 40 from the number.

NOTE

• When a straight shift fails, test letter-reversal (swap) combined with a small shift — common SSC twist.

question:
Select the option that is related to the third letter-number cluster in the same way as the second letter-number cluster is related to the first letter-number cluster and sixth letter-number cluster is related to fifth letter-number cluster. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

RJT120 : TLR240 :: AKY142 : ? :: LMS202 : NOQ404
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. CMW284.

GIVEN

• RJT120 : TLR240 :: AKY142 : ? :: LMS202 : NOQ404

SOLUTION

• RJT120 → TLR240: R+2=T, J+2=L, T−2=R; number 120×2=240.

• Check LMS202 → NOQ404: L+2=N, M+2=O, S−2=Q; 202×2=404. Rule = (+2, +2, −2), number ×2.

• Apply to AKY142: A+2=C, K+2=M, Y−2=W; 142×2=284 → CMW284.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• First two letters +2, third letter −2, number doubled.

NOTE

• Always test both add/subtract on letters and ×/÷/+ on the number to lock the exact rule.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fourth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and fifth number is related to sixth number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

3915 : 3947 :: ? : 3568 :: 87 : 119
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 3536.

GIVEN

• 3915 : 3947 :: ? : 3568 :: 87 : 119

SOLUTION

• First pair: 3947 − 3915 = 32. Third pair: 119 − 87 = 32. So each right number = left number + 32.

• Here the unknown is the LEFT number of its pair, with right number 3568.

• Left = 3568 − 32 = 3536.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• The constant gap is +32; since 3568 is the bigger (right) number, subtract 32 → 3536.

NOTE

• Note which side of the pair is unknown — add or subtract the constant accordingly.

question:
Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and sixth number is related to fifth number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

9373 : 9336 :: 7519 : ? :: 7996 : 7959
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 7482.

GIVEN

• 9373 : 9336 :: 7519 : ? :: 7996 : 7959

SOLUTION

• First pair: 9336 − 9373 = −37. Third pair: 7959 − 7996 = −37. So the second number = first − 37.

• Apply to 7519: 7519 − 37 = 7482.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Constant difference −37; 7519 − 37 = 7482.

NOTE

• A fixed additive/subtractive constant across pairs is the simplest number-analogy pattern — check it first.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and fourth number is related to third number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

17 : 225 :: 22 : 400 :: 27 : ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 625.

GIVEN

• 17 : 225 :: 22 : 400 :: 27 : ?

SOLUTION

• Rule: (number − 2)². 17→(15)²=225; 22→(20)²=400.

• 27→(27−2)² = 25² = 625.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Right term = (left − 2)²; (27−2)² = 625.

NOTE

• When the right value is a perfect square, take its root and compare with the left number to spot the (x−k) pattern.

question: In a certain code language, 'water is important' is coded as 'pq tl fe' and 'save water for future' is coded as 'pm tl fm zp'. How will 'water' be coded in that code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. tl.

GIVEN

• 'water is important' → 'pq tl fe'

• 'save water for future' → 'pm tl fm zp'

SOLUTION

• The only common word between the two sentences is 'water'.

• The only common code between 'pq tl fe' and 'pm tl fm zp' is 'tl'.

• Hence 'water' = tl.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Match the shared word to the shared code — 'water' ↔ 'tl'.

NOTE

• In code questions, the word common to two lines maps to the code common to those two lines.

question: In a certain code language, 'track the eject break' is coded as 'ev ot bb ha', 'break are people blue' is coded as 'ct ha na ma', and 'color are eject text' is coded as 'ma sm ot er'. How will 'color text' be coded in that code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. sm er.

GIVEN

• 'track the eject break' → 'ev ot bb ha'

• 'break are people blue' → 'ct ha na ma'

• 'color are eject text' → 'ma sm ot er'

SOLUTION

• 'break' (lines 1 & 2) → common code 'ha'; 'are' (lines 2 & 3) → common code 'ma'; 'eject' (lines 1 & 3) → common code 'ot'.

• In line 3 'color are eject text' = 'ma sm ot er', removing are(ma) and eject(ot) leaves 'sm' and 'er' for 'color' and 'text'.

• So 'color text' = sm er.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Cancel the already-known codes (are=ma, eject=ot) from line 3; what remains is color+text = sm er.

NOTE

• Solve overlapping code sentences by pairing common words with common codes, then eliminate to isolate the target words.

question:
A series is given with one term wrong. Select that wrong term from the given alternatives.

PT16, UQ25, XP36, BN49, FL64, JJ81
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. UQ25.

GIVEN

• PT16, UQ25, XP36, BN49, FL64, JJ81

SOLUTION

• Numbers 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 81 = 4², 5², 6², 7², 8², 9² (all correct).

• First letters should rise by +4: P(16), T(20), X(24), B(28), F(32), J(36) → 2nd should be T, not U.

• Second letters should fall by −2: T(20), R(18), P(16), N(14), L(12), J(10) → 2nd should be R, not Q.

• So the 2nd term should be TR25, but it is UQ25 — the wrong term.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Columns run +4 (first letter) and −2 (second letter); only UQ25 breaks both — it should be TR25.

NOTE

• For 'find the wrong term', verify each column and the numbers separately; the odd one violates the fixed step.

question:
A series is given with one term wrong. Select that wrong term from the given alternatives.

EAG102, AFN105, WKS106, SPY108, OUE110, KZK112
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. AFN105.

GIVEN

• EAG102, AFN105, WKS106, SPY108, OUE110, KZK112

SOLUTION

• Numbers should increase by +2: 102, 104, 106, 108, 110, 112 → the 2nd should be 104, not 105.

• Third letters run +6: G(7), M(13), S(19), Y(25), E(31), K(37) → 2nd should be M, not N.

• First letters −4 and second letters +5 are consistent elsewhere. So the 2nd term should be AMM104, but it is AFN105 — the wrong term.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• The number column must be even (+2): 102,104,106… so 105 is the giveaway — AFN105 is wrong.

NOTE

• Numbers often expose the wrong term fastest; scan them before decoding every letter column.
